heading: INT. ROLLER RINK - FAMILY REUNION - DAY

units.text: INT. ROLLER RINK - FAMILY REUNION - DAY
A wood-floored rink under a mirror ball.
Banner reads "WASHINGTON FAMILY 40TH."
Folding tables of casserole line one wall.
Disco hits thump faintly.
PEARL WASHINGTON, eighties, in a purple tracksuit, sits on a throne of folding chairs.
UNCLE ROY, sixties, her son, rolls by on rented skates, arms out.
TAMIKA, thirties, Roy's niece, balances a paper plate in one hand and her phone in the other.
JUNIOR, fifteen, hangs on the rail, hoodie up.
LILIANA, six, Tamika's daughter, sits cross-legged on the floor lacing her skates wrong.
Roy! Skate like you got sense!
units.name: PEARL

units.text: I'm skating, Ma!
units.name: UNCLE ROY

units.text: He is not.
He wobbles.
He grabs the rail beside Junior and holds on, grinning.
Junior, take your hood off.
units.name: TAMIKA

units.text: It's fine.
units.name: JUNIOR

units.text: It's your grandmother's birthday.
units.name: TAMIKA

units.text: Junior pushes the hood back an inch.
Tamika sets her plate in front of Pearl, who pushes it back toward Tamika.
That's not my food.
units.name: PEARL

units.text: It's your casserole.
units.name: TAMIKA

units.text: Then why is it cold?
units.name: PEARL

units.text: Liliana tugs Tamika's sleeve.
Mama, my skates are on backwards.
units.name: LILIANA

units.text: They're on your wrong feet, baby.
units.name: TAMIKA

units.text: She kneels.
Roy rolls up and lowers himself beside Pearl, and Pearl, without a word, pats his knee twice.
Junior watches this from the rail and lets the hood fall all the way down.
